documents.markdown:
# Kontour CLI

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40kontourai%2Fcli)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kontourai/cli)
[![CI](https://github.com/kontourai/cli/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/kontourai/cli/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-kontourai.github.io-blue)](https://kontourai.github.io/cli/)
[![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

[Documentation](https://kontourai.github.io/cli/)

**Offline-first suite router for Kontour products.**

`@kontourai/cli` provides the suite-level `kontour` command. It owns navigation, descriptor discovery, diagnostics, and safe subprocess delegation across [Flow](https://kontourai.io/flow), [Flow Agents](https://kontourai.io/flow-agents), and [Console](https://kontourai.io/console). It does not implement product commands, import product kernels, download products, or acquire authority to mutate product state.

> This package was extracted from [`kontourai/console`](https://github.com/kontourai/console) (where it lived at `cli/`) into its own repository because it is a cross-product suite router, not a Console-owned tool. Its only runtime dependency is the shared, exact-pinned [`@kontourai/console-core`](https://github.com/kontourai/console/tree/main/console-core) package. Issue history predating the move remains at `kontourai/console`.

## Install and invoke

Node.js 22 or newer is required. Install the router explicitly:

```sh
npm install --global @kontourai/cli
kontour products
kontour capabilities
kontour doctor
kontour console serve
```

For a one-off invocation, pin the router version and opt into each product package explicitly:

```sh
npx --yes \
  --package @kontourai/cli@<exact-version> \
  --package @kontourai/console@<exact-version> \
  kontour console serve
```

`npx` package flags are installation consent. The router itself never invokes npm, searches a registry, downloads a missing package, or silently changes a version. It resolves sibling product packages from the installed CLI's normal Node package graph. For reproducible and offline work, preinstall exact package versions and retain the npm cache or a lockfile-backed installation. A missing local product produces exact package-level install and one-shot commands rather than a network fallback.

See the [Kontour CLI Router specification](docs/kontour-cli-router.md) for installed discovery, explicit product roots, namespace ownership, transparency/confirmation boundaries, and compatibility-catalog provenance, and [Kontour Init](docs/kontour-init.md) for the `kontour init` onboarding transaction.

## Published package

- `@kontourai/cli` — the offline-first suite router (`kontour` bin) for Flow, Flow Agents, and Console product delegation. Exact-pins `@kontourai/console-core` and validates that pin's registry-visible metadata before every release.

## Development

```sh
npm ci
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run check:import-boundary
npm run build
```

- `npm test` runs the unit/integration suite (`test/*.test.ts`).
- `npm run check:import-boundary` enforces that the router never imports product runtimes, unapproved `@kontourai/console-core` entrypoints, or denied Node built-ins — statically over source, over the compiled `dist` output, and against a negative fixture that must still trip the check.
- `npm run test:tarball` packs the CLI (plus the resolved `@kontourai/console-core` dependency and the three product test fixtures) and smoke-tests the packed artifact fully offline.
- `npm run test:init-e2e` and `npm run test:registry-regression` are network-dependent end-to-end checks against real, published `@kontourai/flow-agents`/`@kontourai/flow`/`@kontourai/cli` versions; they are not part of the default CI gate.

## License

Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

See [documentation maintenance](docs/contributing.md) when changing source or public contracts.

documents.title: Getting started
documents.markdown:
# Getting started

`@kontourai/cli` installs one command, `kontour`. It finds the Kontour product packages you have installed (Flow, Flow Agents, Console) and hands your command to the product that owns it. This page takes you from install to a first delegated command.

## Requirements

Node.js 22 or newer.

## Install

```sh
npm install --global @kontourai/cli
```

The router never installs products for you. Install the ones you want yourself, with exact versions, into the same `node_modules` as the router (see [Installing products](#installing-products)).

## See what the router found

Three read-only commands report on the products. They work offline and change nothing.

```sh
kontour products       # which products are available, missing, or incompatible
kontour capabilities   # the commands, artifacts, and projections each product declares
kontour doctor         # the same report; the text form also prints remediation for anything missing or incompatible
```

Each accepts `--json` for machine-readable output. `capabilities` also accepts one product id (`console`, `flow`, or `flow-agents`) to narrow the report:

```sh
kontour capabilities flow-agents --json
```

A product that is not installed shows as `missing`. `doctor` then prints package-level install commands for the version the router's catalog expects. The JSON output of all three commands carries the same `remediation` lists.

## Run a product command

Put the product's namespace first. The router resolves the product's executable and runs it with your remaining arguments, in your current directory, with your terminal attached.

```sh
kontour console serve
kontour flow status
kontour flow agents workflow status
```

The router only runs commands that the product's descriptor declares. A command that is not declared is refused with `ROUTER_COMMAND_UNKNOWN`. See the [namespace table](kontour-cli-router.md#namespace-and-ownership) for which namespace belongs to which product.

## Installing products

The router looks for each product package in one place: the `node_modules` directory that holds the installed `@kontourai/cli` package, at `<that node_modules>/<package name>`. It does not search `$PATH`, parent directories, home directories, or the network. A router installed globally therefore sees products installed in the same global `node_modules`, not products installed in a project. A package that is a symlink (as with `npm link` or pnpm) is reported as `incompatible`, not found.

For a reproducible setup, install the router and the products together, with exact versions:

```sh
npm install --save-exact @kontourai/cli@<exact-version> @kontourai/console@<exact-version>
```

For a one-off run, name each package on the `npx` command. The `--package` flags are your consent to install; the router itself never runs npm.

```sh
npx --yes \
  --package @kontourai/cli@<exact-version> \
  --package @kontourai/console@<exact-version> \
  kontour console serve
```

If a product lives somewhere the router would not look, point at it with `--product-root`:

```sh
kontour --product-root=console=/absolute/path/to/console-package products
```

## Next steps

- [Concepts](concepts.md) explains descriptors, discovery, delegation, and the compatibility catalog.
- [Reference](reference.md) lists every command, option, error code, and exit code.
- [Kontour Init](kontour-init.md) covers `kontour init`, the onboarding transaction for Flow Agents.

documents.title: Concepts
documents.markdown:
# Concepts

`kontour` is a router, not a product. It owns navigation, discovery, diagnostics, and safe delegation. Everything a command actually does belongs to the product that declares it.

## Products and namespaces

The router knows three products. Each owns a namespace.

| Product id | Package | Namespace |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flow` | `@kontourai/flow` | `kontour flow ...` |
| `flow-agents` | `@kontourai/flow-agents` | `kontour flow agents ...` |
| `console` | `@kontourai/console` | `kontour console ...` |

Namespaces match by longest prefix, so `flow agents` goes to Flow Agents before the general `flow` namespace is considered. The router removes that prefix, matches the rest against the product's declared commands, and runs the declared executable with the descriptor's argument vector followed by whatever you typed after the command. The full table, including the kit commands, is in the [router specification](kontour-cli-router.md#namespace-and-ownership).

## Descriptors

A product describes itself with a capability descriptor: its identity, its executables, and each command it exposes, including the command's side effect (`read-local` or `write-local`, for example) and what confirmation it needs (`never` or `user-request`). `kontour capabilities` shows this metadata. It is transparency, not consent.

A descriptor comes from one of two places:

- **Product-owned.** A package ships `product-capability-descriptor.json`. Its presence always makes it the reported source, even if it fails validation, so a broken product-owned descriptor is reported as a problem rather than silently replaced. The package version must still equal the version the catalog expects.
- **The compatibility catalog.** The router bundles a descriptor for each product, with the package version it was derived from. This is a temporary bridge for products that do not ship their own yet. Each entry records its provenance and a removal trigger.

Every descriptor, from either source, is validated before use. The catalog never supplies executable code or install instructions.

## Discovery

For each product, the router resolves a package root in this order:

1. An explicit `--product-root=<product>=<absolute-root>` option.
2. The package of that name in the `node_modules` directory that holds the installed `@kontourai/cli`. This is a single directory lookup, not a walk up the directory tree, so a project-local product is invisible to a globally installed router.

It then reads that package's own `package.json` to establish the package name, version, and `bin` map. It does not trust the caller's description of the package. A root whose name does not match, or whose version differs from the one the catalog expects, is reported as incompatible. So is an installed package that is a symlink. A product with no root is reported as missing.

Discovery is offline. There is no network fallback.

## Delegation

When you run a product command, the router:

1. Selects the namespace and matches the command against the descriptor.
2. Resolves the declared executable to a real file inside the product package.
3. Runs it as an argument vector with no shell, in your current directory, with your standard streams.
4. Forwards `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` to the child and returns the child's exit code.

The product keeps all authority over its own artifacts, gates, confirmations, exit status, and signal behavior. The router cannot skip a step, grant an exception, or reinterpret a failure.

## Consent and install policy

Showing a command's side effects is not permission to run it. The router never invokes npm, never downloads a missing product, and never changes a version on its own. When a product is missing it prints inert, copy-paste install commands pinned to the exact version the catalog expects; you run them yourself. Tags, ranges, and alternate package sources are not accepted as package specs.

## Init as a transaction

`kontour init` is the one place the router coordinates more than a single command. It builds a deterministic plan from a repository and the installed Flow Agents package, shows it, and applies it only when you pass the plan's SHA-256 id and `--yes`. Each action in the plan is delegated to Flow Agents. See [Kontour Init](kontour-init.md).

## What the router does not do

It does not implement product commands, import product code, host Station, merge packages, authorize side effects, or manage upgrades. Flow, Flow Agents, and Console stay independently usable through their own commands.

documents.markdown:
# Kontour CLI Router

`@kontourai/cli` provides the suite-level `kontour` command. It owns navigation, descriptor discovery, diagnostics, and safe subprocess delegation. It does not implement product commands, import product kernels, download products, or acquire authority to mutate product state.

## Install and invoke

Node.js 22 or newer is required. Install the router explicitly:

```sh
npm install --global @kontourai/cli
kontour products
kontour capabilities
kontour doctor
kontour console serve
```

For a one-off invocation, pin the router version and opt into each product package explicitly:

```sh
npx --yes \
  --package @kontourai/cli@<exact-version> \
  --package @kontourai/console@<exact-version> \
  kontour console serve
```

`npx` package flags are installation consent. The router itself never invokes npm, searches a registry, downloads a missing package, or silently changes a version. It resolves sibling product packages from the installed CLI's normal Node package graph. For reproducible and offline work, preinstall exact package versions and retain the npm cache or a lockfile-backed installation. A missing local product produces exact package-level install and one-shot commands rather than a network fallback.

## Installed discovery and explicit product roots

Product roots use an explicit, repeatable mapping:

```sh
kontour --product-root=flow=/absolute/path/to/flow-package \
        --product-root=flow-agents=/absolute/path/to/flow-agents-package \
        --product-root=console=/absolute/path/to/console-package \
        products
```

Each key selects one exact catalog product/package and each value supplies its local package root. An explicit mapping always wins over installed-package discovery. Without a mapping, the router uses Node package resolution anchored at the installed `@kontourai/cli` package; it does not scan `$PATH`, global npm directories, arbitrary ancestors, home directories, or the network. Resolved manifests and bins pass the same identity, containment, and symlink checks as explicit roots. Product-shipped, validated descriptors take precedence over compatibility entries.

`kontour --help` and `kontour init --help` render before product discovery or repository/setup validation. Both exit zero and write no setup artifacts.

## Namespace and ownership

The suite namespace is deliberately declarative:

| Suite command | Owner and direct bin |
| --- | --- |
| `kontour flow ...` | Flow; direct `flow ...` remains supported. |
| `kontour flow kit validate/install/inspect ...` | Flow kit lifecycle; direct `flow kit ...` remains supported. |
| `kontour flow agents ...` | Flow Agents; direct `flow-agents ...` remains supported. |
| `kontour flow agents kit install/activate/status ...` | Flow Agents kit distribution and activation; Flow does not absorb this lifecycle. |
| `kontour console ...` | Console; `console-inspect` and Console's product bins remain supported. |

Longest-prefix matching gives `flow agents` to Flow Agents before general Flow routing. The router removes only the suite-owned prefix, then passes the descriptor-owned argv and remaining user argv as literal subprocess arguments with the caller's cwd and stdio. Station is intentionally excluded: it is an application and operating environment, not a nested router product.

## Transparency, confirmation, and authority

`products`, `capabilities`, and `doctor` are read-only router commands. They expose descriptor identity, package/version, provenance, protocol compatibility, command side effects, prerequisites, and required confirmation. This is transparency metadata, not consent.

`kontour init` adds an explicit suite onboarding transaction above the router. Inspect and plan are read-only, and plan emits its deterministic artifact and SHA-256 plan id on stdout. Apply recomputes that plan from the same requested state plus live repository and package authority, requires the exact `--plan-id` with explicit `--yes` consent, and then delegates every action to Flow Agents. Saved plan files and output paths are unsupported; `--plan-file` and `--output` are rejected. See [Kontour Init](kontour-init.md). It does not broaden normal router discovery or grant the router product authority.

Every delegated command remains under the named product's authority. The product owns its artifacts, gates, lifecycle, confirmation, exit status, and signal behavior. The router cannot skip a Flow step, synthesize a cancellation, grant an exception, weaken a confirmation rule, or reinterpret a product failure. Cancellation remains a user-requested product operation where the product descriptor says so.

## Compatibility catalog

The packaged compatibility catalog is a temporary, source-attributed bridge for products that do not yet ship a validated descriptor. Every entry records the owning product/package, source version, catalog version, and provenance. Catalog data is inert and passes the same descriptor validation and protocol negotiation as product-owned data; it never supplies executable code or installation instructions.

An entry is removed only after the owning product publishes a validated descriptor covering the supported commands, its release is available through the documented product root, and conformance tests prove equivalent routing and metadata. Removal is per product, not an all-or-nothing catalog retirement. A product-owned descriptor always wins when both sources are present.

## Legacy Console migration

`@kontourai/console` continues to ship its legacy `kontour serve` bin with unchanged server parsing and behavior during the compatibility window. New suite usage should install `@kontourai/cli` and invoke:

```sh
kontour console serve
```

The legacy alias is deprecated but will not be removed before Console 3.0. Removal additionally requires a released router migration path, published documentation, and compatibility evidence for the delegated Console command. The legacy bin does not proxy through the router.

## Safety and non-goals

Delegation uses a validated descriptor, a Node-resolved or explicitly supplied contained package bin, an argv array, and no shell. Discovery and diagnostic commands are offline. The router does not merge packages, host Station, implement server behavior, authorize side effects, manage product upgrades, or replace the independently usable Flow, Flow Agents, and Console CLIs.

documents.title: Reference
documents.markdown:
# Reference

## Command line

```text
kontour [--product-root=<product>=<absolute-root>]... <command> [options]
```

### Router options

#### --product-root

`--product-root=<product>=<absolute-root>` points the router at a product package. `<product>` is `flow`, `flow-agents`, or `console`, and the root must be an absolute path. Give at most one root per product. The option is accepted only before the command, and it overrides installed-package discovery.

#### --help

`--help` and `-h` print usage and exit `0` when they are the first token after any `--product-root` options. `kontour init --help` prints the `init` usage. Help renders before any product discovery or root validation. After a built-in command, `--help` is not help: `kontour products --help` exits `2`. After a product command it is passed through to the product.

### Built-in commands

| Command | Arguments | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kontour products` | `[--json]` | Lists each product with its package, version, availability, protocol compatibility, and descriptor source. |
| `kontour capabilities` | `[flow\|flow-agents\|console] [--json]` | As `products`, plus each product's commands (side effect and confirmation), artifacts, and projections. A product id narrows the report. |
| `kontour doctor` | `[--json]` | As `products`, plus remediation commands for missing or incompatible products. |
| `kontour init` | see below | Inspect, plan, or apply a pinned Flow Agents setup. |

`products` and `doctor` accept only `--json`. `--json` may appear anywhere after the command. `--online` is reserved and refused with `ROUTER_ARGUMENT_INVALID`: the router performs no network access.

Availability is `available`, `missing`, or `incompatible`. Output carries a `schemaVersion`, the `command`, a list of `products`, and a flat list of `diagnostics`. The JSON shape is published as `schemas/router-output.schema.json`.

### init

```text
kontour init <--inspect|--plan|--apply> [--runtime <runtime>] [--kit <id>]... [--plan-id <sha256>] [--yes] [--json]
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--inspect` | Run read-only Flow Agents diagnostics and report. |
| `--plan` | Compute the deterministic plan and its SHA-256 id. Writes nothing. |
| `--apply` | Run the approved plan. Requires `--plan-id` and `--yes`. |
| `--runtime` | One of `base`, `codex`, `claude-code`, `kiro`, `opencode`, `pi`. Default `codex`. |
| `--kit` | A kit catalog id: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, up to 64 characters, starting with a letter or digit. Repeatable; duplicates are removed. Default none. |
| `--plan-id` | The id from `--plan`. Must match the live repository and package state. |
| `--yes` | Explicit consent to apply. |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output. |

Exactly one of `--inspect`, `--plan`, `--apply` is required. The behavior, consent model, and failure handling are described in [Kontour Init](kontour-init.md).

### Delegated commands

Any other command is matched against the namespaces in the [router specification](kontour-cli-router.md#namespace-and-ownership). The commands each product declares in the bundled compatibility catalog are:

| Namespace | Commands |
| --- | --- |
| `kontour console` | `inspect`, `serve` |
| `kontour flow` | `status`, `start`, `cancel`, `kit validate`, `kit install`, `kit inspect` |
| `kontour flow agents` | `init`, `telemetry-doctor`, `workflow status`, `workflow start`, `workflow cancel`, `kit install`, `kit activate`, `kit status` |

A product that ships its own descriptor takes over as the reported source, but only when its package version equals the version the catalog expects. Run `kontour capabilities` to see what your installation exposes. A descriptor's declared argument vector replaces the matched command words, so `kontour console inspect` runs Console's `console-inspect` bin with no `inspect` argument.

## Limits

The router refuses a command line with more than 256 tokens, a token longer than 4096 characters, or a token containing a NUL, carriage return, or newline. The refusal is `ROUTER_ARGUMENT_INVALID`.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Success, including help. |
| `2` | The router refused or could not route the request (diagnostics are written to stderr as `CODE: message`). |
| `70` | An internal error (`KONTOUR_INTERNAL_ERROR`). |
| other | For a delegated command, the product's own exit code. If the product is ended by a signal, `128` plus the signal number. |

`kontour init --apply` returns the exit code of the first failed action, or `0`.

## Diagnostic codes

| Code | Raised when |
| --- | --- |
| `ROUTER_ARGUMENT_INVALID` | Bad or duplicate `--product-root`, oversized arguments, `--online`, or extra arguments to `products` or `doctor`. |
| `ROUTER_NAMESPACE_UNKNOWN` | The first words are not `flow`, `flow agents`, or `console`. |
| `ROUTER_COMMAND_UNKNOWN` | The product's descriptor does not declare the command. |
| `ROUTER_PRODUCT_UNKNOWN` | `capabilities` was given something other than a product id. |
| `ROUTER_PRODUCT_MISSING` | A warning in `products`, `capabilities`, and `doctor` output: no installed package was found for the product. |
| `DESCRIPTOR_EXECUTABLE_MISSING` | You delegated to a product that is not installed. The message gives install commands. |
| `DESCRIPTOR_MALFORMED` | An installed product failed identity, version, or descriptor checks (wrong package name, a version other than the catalog's, a symlinked root, a bad descriptor). Delegation is refused and the product shows as `incompatible`. |
| `KONTOUR_DELEGATION_SPAWN_FAILED` | The product executable could not be started. |

`init` adds:

- `KONTOUR_INIT_ARGUMENT_INVALID`: no mode or more than one, an unknown token, or a bad runtime or kit id.
- `KONTOUR_INIT_FLOW_AGENTS_REQUIRED`: Flow Agents is missing or incompatible.
- `KONTOUR_INIT_EXACT_VERSION_REQUIRED`: Flow Agents, or the Flow package it depends on, is not the pinned version.
- `KONTOUR_INIT_CONSENT_REQUIRED`: `--apply` without `--yes` or without `--plan-id`.
- `KONTOUR_INIT_PLAN_INVALID`: the plan id no longer matches live repository and package state.
- `KONTOUR_INIT_REPOSITORY_DRIFT`: the repository changed identity before execution.

An unexpected failure while reading the Flow Agents package graph (for example a declared dependency that is not installed) surfaces as `KONTOUR_INTERNAL_ERROR` with exit `70`.

## Package exports

`@kontourai/cli` is CommonJS and exports:

- The root entry (`dist/index.js`, with types). It exposes `runCli`, the routing and discovery functions (`parseCommandLine`, `selectNamespace`, `routeCommand`, `discoverProducts`, `discoverFromOptions`, `resolveDiscoveredExecutable`), the output builders (`buildRouterOutput`, `renderRouterOutput`), the help helpers (`helpScope`, `renderHelp`), the install-policy validators (`validateExactPackageSpec`, `validateExplicitDownloadSpecs`, `missingProductRemediation`), the `compatibilityCatalog` and its version constants, the output comparators, and the standalone runner (`createStandaloneRunner`, `resolveStandaloneProductBinding`, `StandaloneRunnerExecutionError`). `src/index.ts` is the authoritative list.
- `@kontourai/cli/schemas/router-output.schema.json`, the JSON Schema for `products`, `capabilities`, and `doctor` output.
- `@kontourai/cli/schemas/init-plan.schema.json`, the JSON Schema for the `init` plan.

The package ships one executable, `kontour`.

documents.title: Kontour Init
documents.markdown:
# Kontour Init

`kontour init` is a suite-level onboarding transaction planner. It shows how a repository would be configured and delegates approved actions to the product that owns them. It does not implement Flow Agents runtime, provider, power, doctor, or kit semantics.

Use exact, explicitly installed product roots. Each plan identifies the exact version of the installed `@kontourai/cli` package that is executing it. The product contract separately pins `@kontourai/console@2.5.0`, `@kontourai/flow-agents@3.8.0`, and `@kontourai/flow@3.1.4`.

```sh
kontour --product-root=flow-agents=/absolute/path/to/node_modules/@kontourai/flow-agents \
  init --inspect --json

kontour --product-root=flow-agents=/absolute/path/to/node_modules/@kontourai/flow-agents \
  init --plan --runtime codex --kit builder --json

kontour --product-root=flow-agents=/absolute/path/to/node_modules/@kontourai/flow-agents \
  init --apply --runtime codex --kit builder --plan-id <sha256> --yes --json
```

Exactly one of `--inspect`, `--plan`, or `--apply` is required. All modes support JSON. Plan output is deterministic for the same repository, desired state, and exact product version.

## No implicit kits

The desired kit list defaults to empty. A plan without `--kit` passes no kit activation flags to Flow Agents. Builder is activated only when the caller explicitly supplies `--kit builder`. Kontour does not maintain its own kit catalog or infer a kit from the repository.

## Consent and mutation

Inspect delegates only released read-only Flow Agents diagnostics (`telemetry-doctor` and `kit status`) and preserves their structured output and exit status. Plan performs no product delegation and writes nothing: the approved plan id is emitted on stdout. Apply recomputes the plan from the same explicit runtime and kit inputs plus live canonical repository/package state; saved plan files and output paths are deliberately unsupported.

Apply requires the SHA-256 plan id and `--yes`. Before delegation it recomputes the canonical repository identity; the exact `process.execPath` interpreter identity and bytes; and deterministic content digests for every realpath-identified Flow Agents package instance plus its actually loadable dependency, optional-dependency, and peer-dependency graph, including Flow. Duplicate package names at different realpaths/versions remain distinct graph nodes. Verified package instances are copied into a self-contained private store, rehashed, and connected only with internally generated links that reproduce the approved topology. The verified Node binary is copied too and invoked directly with the JavaScript entrypoint, so neither shebang resolution nor `PATH` selects the interpreter. All private material is removed in `finally`.

Immediately before the first action, Kontour enters the canonical repository directory and compares `.` to the already-open directory descriptor. Delegated children inherit that held cwd without a new pathname lookup, so a later rename cannot redirect subsequent actions into a replacement directory. Every action identifies its product owner, literal argv vector, side-effect class, expected paths, postcondition, and recovery instruction. Delegation uses an argv array and no shell.

Actions run in order. A failure stops the sequence: later actions are `not_run`, and the result includes recovery instructions for actions that actually ran. Kontour performs no automatic rollback, does not claim a cross-product transaction, and does not delete unknown files. Follow Flow Agents-owned lifecycle guidance and restore only material whose provenance you have independently confirmed.

## Product-owned gaps

Flow Agents owns unified doctor findings, provider discovery/settings, runtime detection, policy settings, powers/MCP registration, tokens, kit catalog behavior, and validators. Until those capabilities are exposed by a compatible released Flow Agents descriptor, inspect reports them as unsupported or not verified with their upstream issue references. Console does not substitute its own checks or writers.

Public npm bootstrap verification remains required whenever the exact `@kontourai/cli` release is not registry-visible. A local packed-package E2E is useful implementation evidence but is not a substitute for that release check.

# Documentation maintenance

`corpus.json` routes CLI implementation and schema changes to the command/API
reference, and initialization changes to its setup guide. Review those claims
against their real callers when changing the selected inputs.

Run the shared Corpus gate against `origin/main`. Update inaccurate prose in the
same PR. If it remains accurate, add a new local input/output byte review with
an explanation and limits in `corpus-content.json`, following
[Corpus's review contract](https://github.com/kontourai/corpus/blob/b127e35a818b532369843731b3c64792baade83e/docs/related-content.md#review-an-unchanged-covering-document).
Use that same reviewed Corpus revision for local checks. A hash match does not
prove that prose is true; do not refresh hashes without inspecting the change.

topics.title: Install the router and products
topics.markdown:
## Installing products

The router looks for each product package in one place: the `node_modules` directory that holds the installed `@kontourai/cli` package, at `<that node_modules>/<package name>`. It does not search `$PATH`, parent directories, home directories, or the network. A router installed globally therefore sees products installed in the same global `node_modules`, not products installed in a project. A package that is a symlink (as with `npm link` or pnpm) is reported as `incompatible`, not found.

For a reproducible setup, install the router and the products together, with exact versions:

```sh
npm install --save-exact @kontourai/cli@<exact-version> @kontourai/console@<exact-version>
```

For a one-off run, name each package on the `npx` command. The `--package` flags are your consent to install; the router itself never runs npm.

```sh
npx --yes \
  --package @kontourai/cli@<exact-version> \
  --package @kontourai/console@<exact-version> \
  kontour console serve
```

If a product lives somewhere the router would not look, point at it with `--product-root`:

```sh
kontour --product-root=console=/absolute/path/to/console-package products
```

topics.title: Products and namespaces
topics.markdown:
## Products and namespaces

The router knows three products. Each owns a namespace.

| Product id | Package | Namespace |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flow` | `@kontourai/flow` | `kontour flow ...` |
| `flow-agents` | `@kontourai/flow-agents` | `kontour flow agents ...` |
| `console` | `@kontourai/console` | `kontour console ...` |

Namespaces match by longest prefix, so `flow agents` goes to Flow Agents before the general `flow` namespace is considered. The router removes that prefix, matches the rest against the product's declared commands, and runs the declared executable with the descriptor's argument vector followed by whatever you typed after the command. The full table, including the kit commands, is in the [router specification](kontour-cli-router.md#namespace-and-ownership).

topics.title: Product descriptors
topics.markdown:
## Descriptors

A product describes itself with a capability descriptor: its identity, its executables, and each command it exposes, including the command's side effect (`read-local` or `write-local`, for example) and what confirmation it needs (`never` or `user-request`). `kontour capabilities` shows this metadata. It is transparency, not consent.

A descriptor comes from one of two places:

- **Product-owned.** A package ships `product-capability-descriptor.json`. Its presence always makes it the reported source, even if it fails validation, so a broken product-owned descriptor is reported as a problem rather than silently replaced. The package version must still equal the version the catalog expects.
- **The compatibility catalog.** The router bundles a descriptor for each product, with the package version it was derived from. This is a temporary bridge for products that do not ship their own yet. Each entry records its provenance and a removal trigger.

Every descriptor, from either source, is validated before use. The catalog never supplies executable code or install instructions.

topics.title: Product discovery
topics.markdown:
## Discovery

For each product, the router resolves a package root in this order:

1. An explicit `--product-root=<product>=<absolute-root>` option.
2. The package of that name in the `node_modules` directory that holds the installed `@kontourai/cli`. This is a single directory lookup, not a walk up the directory tree, so a project-local product is invisible to a globally installed router.

It then reads that package's own `package.json` to establish the package name, version, and `bin` map. It does not trust the caller's description of the package. A root whose name does not match, or whose version differs from the one the catalog expects, is reported as incompatible. So is an installed package that is a symlink. A product with no root is reported as missing.

Discovery is offline. There is no network fallback.

topics.title: How commands are delegated
topics.markdown:
## Delegation

When you run a product command, the router:

1. Selects the namespace and matches the command against the descriptor.
2. Resolves the declared executable to a real file inside the product package.
3. Runs it as an argument vector with no shell, in your current directory, with your standard streams.
4. Forwards `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` to the child and returns the child's exit code.

The product keeps all authority over its own artifacts, gates, confirmations, exit status, and signal behavior. The router cannot skip a step, grant an exception, or reinterpret a failure.

topics.title: Built-in commands
topics.markdown:
### Built-in commands

| Command | Arguments | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kontour products` | `[--json]` | Lists each product with its package, version, availability, protocol compatibility, and descriptor source. |
| `kontour capabilities` | `[flow\|flow-agents\|console] [--json]` | As `products`, plus each product's commands (side effect and confirmation), artifacts, and projections. A product id narrows the report. |
| `kontour doctor` | `[--json]` | As `products`, plus remediation commands for missing or incompatible products. |
| `kontour init` | see below | Inspect, plan, or apply a pinned Flow Agents setup. |

`products` and `doctor` accept only `--json`. `--json` may appear anywhere after the command. `--online` is reserved and refused with `ROUTER_ARGUMENT_INVALID`: the router performs no network access.

Availability is `available`, `missing`, or `incompatible`. Output carries a `schemaVersion`, the `command`, a list of `products`, and a flat list of `diagnostics`. The JSON shape is published as `schemas/router-output.schema.json`.

topics.title: kontour init options
topics.markdown:
### init

```text
kontour init <--inspect|--plan|--apply> [--runtime <runtime>] [--kit <id>]... [--plan-id <sha256>] [--yes] [--json]
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--inspect` | Run read-only Flow Agents diagnostics and report. |
| `--plan` | Compute the deterministic plan and its SHA-256 id. Writes nothing. |
| `--apply` | Run the approved plan. Requires `--plan-id` and `--yes`. |
| `--runtime` | One of `base`, `codex`, `claude-code`, `kiro`, `opencode`, `pi`. Default `codex`. |
| `--kit` | A kit catalog id: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, up to 64 characters, starting with a letter or digit. Repeatable; duplicates are removed. Default none. |
| `--plan-id` | The id from `--plan`. Must match the live repository and package state. |
| `--yes` | Explicit consent to apply. |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output. |

Exactly one of `--inspect`, `--plan`, `--apply` is required. The behavior, consent model, and failure handling are described in [Kontour Init](kontour-init.md).

topics.title: Init consent and mutation
topics.markdown:
## Consent and mutation

Inspect delegates only released read-only Flow Agents diagnostics (`telemetry-doctor` and `kit status`) and preserves their structured output and exit status. Plan performs no product delegation and writes nothing: the approved plan id is emitted on stdout. Apply recomputes the plan from the same explicit runtime and kit inputs plus live canonical repository/package state; saved plan files and output paths are deliberately unsupported.

Apply requires the SHA-256 plan id and `--yes`. Before delegation it recomputes the canonical repository identity; the exact `process.execPath` interpreter identity and bytes; and deterministic content digests for every realpath-identified Flow Agents package instance plus its actually loadable dependency, optional-dependency, and peer-dependency graph, including Flow. Duplicate package names at different realpaths/versions remain distinct graph nodes. Verified package instances are copied into a self-contained private store, rehashed, and connected only with internally generated links that reproduce the approved topology. The verified Node binary is copied too and invoked directly with the JavaScript entrypoint, so neither shebang resolution nor `PATH` selects the interpreter. All private material is removed in `finally`.

Immediately before the first action, Kontour enters the canonical repository directory and compares `.` to the already-open directory descriptor. Delegated children inherit that held cwd without a new pathname lookup, so a later rename cannot redirect subsequent actions into a replacement directory. Every action identifies its product owner, literal argv vector, side-effect class, expected paths, postcondition, and recovery instruction. Delegation uses an argv array and no shell.

Actions run in order. A failure stops the sequence: later actions are `not_run`, and the result includes recovery instructions for actions that actually ran. Kontour performs no automatic rollback, does not claim a cross-product transaction, and does not delete unknown files. Follow Flow Agents-owned lifecycle guidance and restore only material whose provenance you have independently confirmed.

topics.title: Exit codes
topics.markdown:
## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Success, including help. |
| `2` | The router refused or could not route the request (diagnostics are written to stderr as `CODE: message`). |
| `70` | An internal error (`KONTOUR_INTERNAL_ERROR`). |
| other | For a delegated command, the product's own exit code. If the product is ended by a signal, `128` plus the signal number. |

`kontour init --apply` returns the exit code of the first failed action, or `0`.

topics.title: Diagnostic codes
topics.markdown:
## Diagnostic codes

| Code | Raised when |
| --- | --- |
| `ROUTER_ARGUMENT_INVALID` | Bad or duplicate `--product-root`, oversized arguments, `--online`, or extra arguments to `products` or `doctor`. |
| `ROUTER_NAMESPACE_UNKNOWN` | The first words are not `flow`, `flow agents`, or `console`. |
| `ROUTER_COMMAND_UNKNOWN` | The product's descriptor does not declare the command. |
| `ROUTER_PRODUCT_UNKNOWN` | `capabilities` was given something other than a product id. |
| `ROUTER_PRODUCT_MISSING` | A warning in `products`, `capabilities`, and `doctor` output: no installed package was found for the product. |
| `DESCRIPTOR_EXECUTABLE_MISSING` | You delegated to a product that is not installed. The message gives install commands. |
| `DESCRIPTOR_MALFORMED` | An installed product failed identity, version, or descriptor checks (wrong package name, a version other than the catalog's, a symlinked root, a bad descriptor). Delegation is refused and the product shows as `incompatible`. |
| `KONTOUR_DELEGATION_SPAWN_FAILED` | The product executable could not be started. |

`init` adds:

- `KONTOUR_INIT_ARGUMENT_INVALID`: no mode or more than one, an unknown token, or a bad runtime or kit id.
- `KONTOUR_INIT_FLOW_AGENTS_REQUIRED`: Flow Agents is missing or incompatible.
- `KONTOUR_INIT_EXACT_VERSION_REQUIRED`: Flow Agents, or the Flow package it depends on, is not the pinned version.
- `KONTOUR_INIT_CONSENT_REQUIRED`: `--apply` without `--yes` or without `--plan-id`.
- `KONTOUR_INIT_PLAN_INVALID`: the plan id no longer matches live repository and package state.
- `KONTOUR_INIT_REPOSITORY_DRIFT`: the repository changed identity before execution.

An unexpected failure while reading the Flow Agents package graph (for example a declared dependency that is not installed) surfaces as `KONTOUR_INTERNAL_ERROR` with exit `70`.

topics.title: Compatibility catalog
topics.markdown:
## Compatibility catalog

The packaged compatibility catalog is a temporary, source-attributed bridge for products that do not yet ship a validated descriptor. Every entry records the owning product/package, source version, catalog version, and provenance. Catalog data is inert and passes the same descriptor validation and protocol negotiation as product-owned data; it never supplies executable code or installation instructions.

An entry is removed only after the owning product publishes a validated descriptor covering the supported commands, its release is available through the documented product root, and conformance tests prove equivalent routing and metadata. Removal is per product, not an all-or-nothing catalog retirement. A product-owned descriptor always wins when both sources are present.

topics.title: Package exports
topics.markdown:
## Package exports

`@kontourai/cli` is CommonJS and exports:

- The root entry (`dist/index.js`, with types). It exposes `runCli`, the routing and discovery functions (`parseCommandLine`, `selectNamespace`, `routeCommand`, `discoverProducts`, `discoverFromOptions`, `resolveDiscoveredExecutable`), the output builders (`buildRouterOutput`, `renderRouterOutput`), the help helpers (`helpScope`, `renderHelp`), the install-policy validators (`validateExactPackageSpec`, `validateExplicitDownloadSpecs`, `missingProductRemediation`), the `compatibilityCatalog` and its version constants, the output comparators, and the standalone runner (`createStandaloneRunner`, `resolveStandaloneProductBinding`, `StandaloneRunnerExecutionError`). `src/index.ts` is the authoritative list.
- `@kontourai/cli/schemas/router-output.schema.json`, the JSON Schema for `products`, `capabilities`, and `doctor` output.
- `@kontourai/cli/schemas/init-plan.schema.json`, the JSON Schema for the `init` plan.

The package ships one executable, `kontour`.
